summary: The note profiles the Anytown Community Arts Collective (ACAC), founded by former professional dancer Maria Lopez, which has run educational outreach and inclusive theatre and dance programs since September 2023. It shares stories from participants such as Jamal Taylor, Elizabeth Nguyen and Evelyn Smith, and describes inclusivity measures, public performances and intergenerational programs. It closes with ACAC's plans to expand, including a traveling troupe and more school partnerships.
one_line: Anytown Community Arts Collective, founded by Maria Lopez, uses inclusive theatre and dance outreach to build confidence, connection and community across ages and backgrounds.
key_facts: The Anytown Community Arts Collective (ACAC) was founded by Maria Lopez, its founder and artistic director, and has been running outreach and inclusive performance initiatives since September 2023.
Maria Lopez began her performing arts outreach work after a career as a professional dancer.
ACAC's studio is a refurbished downtown space that once lay abandoned.

ACAC began as an effort to provide arts access to underprivileged youth and grew to include people of all ages; it runs after-school programs, weekend workshops and free performances in public spaces.
ACAC collaborates with local schools to integrate theatre and dance into their curriculum.
Jamal Taylor, 15, discovered his love of dance through an ACAC workshop and says dancing is 'like finding a language I didn't know I could speak.'
ACAC offers scholarships, free community performances and 'pay what you can' admission to ensure accessibility regardless of socio-economic status or cultural background.
Elizabeth Nguyen, a Vietnamese immigrant, first attended an ACAC performance in November 2023, felt the play about family, loss and hope 'was telling my story,' and then joined a theatre workshop.
ACAC holds performances in public parks, community centers and local festivals.
Local business owner Michael O'Connor, a regular supporter of ACAC's street performances, says they add vibrancy to the neighborhood and are 'community-building in the truest sense.'
The intergenerational dance series 'Steps Across Time' brings seniors and youth together; 70-year-old participant Evelyn Smith calls it 'magical.'
ACAC hopes to create a traveling troupe for remote or underrepresented areas and to partner with more schools, offering teacher training and curriculum development.
